1539.note: The CHM calendar distinguishes the two neighbouring Eustis letters: item 93 (10 May 1809) is 'part of message in cypher' (already catalogue entry 1538), while item 91 (4 May 1809) is 'Routine; receipt of ciphered message; most necessary for U.S. to maintain friendly relations with neighboring colonies', i.e. Eustis acknowledging a ciphered message from Wilkinson. Nothing says item 91 itself carries cipher, so it is closed as not a cipher text; the ciphered message it acknowledges is Wilkinson's, not in this volume as far as the calendar shows.

1542.note: Not assessed: the blocker of 3 Nov stands. The CHM Primo record gives only '7 military telegraph cipher notebooks used by Fuller and William Rattle Plum' and Fuller's letterpress copies (389 pp.); Union Military Telegraph operators' 'cipher books' were normally the route-cipher key books, whose systems are published (Plum 1882; the Stager/Eckert books), so the notebooks are probably key material, and any enciphered telegrams in them would be readable with published keys. Neither not_cipher nor key_lookup can be proved without seeing a notebook.
